title: How Do Restrictions on Advertising Affect Consumer Search?
eligible_reason: No staggered adoption. The design compares pharmaceutical versus other websites (and pharmaceutical versus medical-device keywords) before and after a single common date, the FDA's March 26, 2009 warning letters to 14 pharmaceutical companies (afterfda = 1 for months after March 2009; sample Feb-Jun 2009). One adoption date, so no eligible specification. Click data (comScore Search Planner, Kantar) are licensed and not shipped.
design_notes: pharma_regressions.do: xi: areg clicks_prop afterfda##pharma afterfda##dodgysite afterfda##infosite afterfda##usersite afterfda##othersite $indicators, cluster($cluster) absorb(mediagroup); also paid/organic reshaped versions with afterfda##type triple interactions. googletrends.do: reg depvar afterfda i.searchterm_id, robust. All treated groups switch on at the same month (post-March 2009), with several treatment-group interactions in each column.
data_files_note: README: data sources are comScore Search Planner, Google Trends and Kantar Media; comScore and Kantar require a license. Only an auxiliary site list and the MTurk survey are shipped.
data_provenance_note: Licensed comScore/Kantar click and ad data not included.
screener_notes: Published PDF text read (data/text/mnsc/mnsc.2021.3980.txt): data span Feb-Jun 2009; Post-FDA indicates months after the March 2009 FDA enforcement change.
